newsitem.title: USA: Transkaryotic partner filed IND application.
newsitem.headline: Transkaryotic partner filed IND application.

text.p: Transkaryotic Therapies Inc said Thursday that Hoechst Marion Roussel Inc, its collaborative partner and a unit of Hoechst AG, has filed an investigational new drug application with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration to commence Phase I clinical trials of gene activated erythropoietin (GA-EPO), for the treatment of anemia.
The company said that submission of the application results in a $2 million milestone payment to Transkaryotic from Hoechst Marion Roussel.

To date, Transkaryotic said it has earned $24 million in payments from Hoechst Marion Roussel relating to the GA-EPO program, and an additional $34 million may be received based on the achievement of certain development milestones.
The company said it expects the clinical trials of GA-EPO to be carried out in a focused and timely manner.
